title: prosiform fixture manifest
description: The declaration of one corpus fixture: the source tree it bundles, the invocation to run against that tree, and the bundles, exit status and diagnostics the run must produce. A runner decides the fixture's result from this declaration and the fixture's files alone. Nothing here names an implementation, a module or a language. The manifest is written as TOML and validated against this document after parsing, because TOML's value model is a subset of JSON's.

description.description: What this fixture establishes, in one sentence.

clauses.description: The design clauses this fixture encodes, each named by its heading and the rule under it, so every clause can be mapped to the fixtures that cover it.

awaiting.description: The work that delivers the behaviour this fixture declares, named as an initiative and an epic and optionally the task within it, such as I00:E03 or I00:E03:W02. A fixture carrying it declares behaviour the build does not yet meet: its failure leaves the corpus run green, and a run in which it meets its manifest fails instead, so the marker is lifted on the change that makes it untrue. A fixture the build is expected to satisfy carries no awaiting.

fault.description: The fault the run performs on itself, which the runner asks for as the contract's `-x NAME`. Three of the outcomes the contract declares are facts about the run rather than about any document it reads, so no source tree states them: `source-changed` writes other bytes to each source the run read, once discovery has read them and before the recheck before publication, `internal` fails the run in itself once the candidate is built and before anything publishes, and `cleanup-refused` stands an empty earlier set at the run's folder and refuses its removal once the new set stands. The fault changes the tree the fixture holds, so a fixture declaring one runs in a copy of itself. A fixture declaring none declares a run that meets no fault.

invocation.description: Working directory and arguments for the configured build, with JSON diagnostics supplied by the runner. The runner names no output folder, so the run writes where these arguments send it: the working directory, or the folder an -o argument names.

arguments.description: Command arguments, in order. The runner supplies JSON diagnostics, except to a fixture declaring no argument and no fault, which runs the bare command.

cwd.description: Existing fixture-relative working directory for the invocation. Omitted, the fixture directory is used.

expected.description: The complete result the run must produce. A comparison that reads one part of it passes a run that failed in another, so every part is declared: the bundles the run writes, its exit status and its diagnostics. Every file the run creates under the fixture or its working directory is compared by name with the bundles declared, so a run writing a file no bundle names fails. Standard output carries no bundle: it is empty unless the text it carries is declared.

exit_status.description: The process exit status, one of the five categories the contract declares: 0 success, 1 input, dependency, policy, safety or resource-limit failure, 2 invalid usage, 3 publication or delivery failure, 4 unexpected internal error.

bundles.description: The fixture-relative paths to the bytes of each bundle the run must write, each file named as the run names the bundle. A run writing no bundle declares none.

stdout_contains.description: The text standard output must carry, where the whole of the response is a build's own. An informational response reporting a version is such a run: the version belongs to the implementation, and what the contract states is the rest. Declared absent, standard output carries nothing.

diagnostics.description: The diagnostics the run must emit on standard error, in order. A run emitting none declares an empty list.

diagnostic.description: One message the run emits to standard error. Its severity and its code name it together, and the severity decides which catalogue the code is drawn from: an error decides a failing run and a warning accompanies a successful one, so neither catalogue admits the other's codes.

severity.description: Whether the message fails the run or accompanies it.

code.description: The stable code naming this diagnostic, from the catalogue its severity selects.

message_contains.description: The text the diagnostic's message carries, declared where the code alone does not identify the fault. One code naming several distinct faults is told apart here: a fixture states the part of the message that identifies its own fault, and each build keeps its own phrasing. A diagnostic declaring none states nothing about its message.

reference.description: The original reference the diagnostic concerns, as the source spells it.

resolved.description: The identity the reference resolved to: the canonical source path of the document it names.

source.description: The referring source location, as a fixture-root-relative path and an optional line.

chain.description: The inclusion chain that reached the reference: the identity of each reference followed from an entry reference, in order, the one this diagnostic concerns last. An entry reference stands at the head of a chain of one.

carriedText.description: Text an output must carry: each entry is a substring that must appear in it. A substring states what identifies the outcome and leaves the wording around it to the build, which is what a comparison of the whole cannot do. One shape serves every such declaration, so a run's output and a diagnostic's message are stated the same way.

fixturePath.description: A path inside the fixture directory: forward slashes, no leading slash, and no parent segment, so a fixture reaches nothing outside itself.

bundlePath.description: A bundle the fixture expects, held under expected/ and named as the run names it in its folder: each selection's name, the names joined with + when a run has several entries, then .bundle.md.

errorCode.description: The error catalogue: the stable error codes the design declares, each prefixed E_. Each is the name of a failure the contract defines, so a fixture cannot expect one it does not. A diagnostic whose severity is error draws its code from here.

warningCode.description: The warning catalogue: the stable warning codes the design declares, each prefixed W_. A warning accompanies a successful run rather than deciding a failing one, so a fixture declaring one states what a run writes to standard error while still succeeding. A diagnostic whose severity is warning draws its code from here.
